execution: Use independent agents with fresh context (no inherited conversation) and no skills activated. Supply only each author task and raw materials. For the candidate condition, provide the relevant instructions from the package under test as a plain editorial brief, not by activating a skill or loading an installed copy. For the baseline condition, omit the brief. Keep this fixture and its rubrics outside writer contexts. A separate fresh agent with no skills activated compares anonymized outputs against the author task, without the candidate brief or intended winner. Record actual deliverables and tool/file actions; activation and attention cannot be inferred from prose alone.
scoring: Judge argument quality, fidelity to the supplied research, directness, and usefulness for the requested article. A candidate must preserve every required outcome and produce no forbidden outcome; those checks alone do not demonstrate improvement over baseline. Compare outputs semantically, allow ties, and report regressions. Assess attention from actions as well as output: unrelated code inspection, workflow artifacts, and verification ceremony count against the requested writing focus. Small paired evaluations are diagnostic, not proof of general superiority.
